item_taken.first_six_words: Own hand, stranger's reasons: the reasoner's
item_taken.why: The department's own earlier artifact, the share's definition, sits exact and complete in the dashboard configuration and in the register, and the reasons for it, the P-versus-Q prediction, were written only in a project board that was decommissioned without export, so Okafor, who is the same institution as the 2017 committee with a closing between, meets the department's own deliberate choice as a stranger's and drafts its retirement as a fix, 'legacy indicator, purpose not recorded, recommend retire', which is this item's tell verbatim; not Hearsay in the window (14), since the register marks the source of the definition, hospital, date, and officer, and what is missing is not whose sentence it is but why; not Record on appeal (11), since no rule forbids the reasons, they are gone; not Report without workpapers (9), since no transcript or workpapers exist anywhere to fetch; not No door in the wall (17), since Okafor perceives the edge and writes 'purpose not recorded'.

reasoning: The rule's axis is whether an arrangement exists that keeps a trace's source readable. The case holds one: the State Health Register under Rule 14, kept by the state, readable by hospitals but not editable or deletable by them, every entry carrying the filing hospital, the date, and the filing officer's name, so that in August 2025 Okafor reads the definition and knows, from the arrangement and not from inference, that Alder Regional filed it and Lindqvist signed it on 3 November 2017. Nothing in the case arrives flat; no sentence's source has to be guessed from register. So the rule as written places the case on the witness-architectures side, as Arm's-length custody, and it leaves here. Residue the rule does not address and I do not carry across as a claim: the arrangement keeps the definition's source readable and was never built to hold its purpose, which is the loss item 15 held; the rule sorts on source, not purpose, so the case crosses on its custody arrangement while the thing it actually lacks, the reason for the indicator, travels along unsorted.
case_out: An arrangement built so that a quality indicator's definition and its source leave a trace that the filing hospital cannot later alter: the State Health Register under Rule 14, kept by the state, readable by hospitals but not editable or deletable by them, every entry carrying the filing hospital, the date, and the filing officer's name. Alder Regional Hospital's emergency department chose its triage protocol in 2017; the Triage Selection Committee, three clinicians, weighed Protocol Q, a five-level triage, against Protocol P, a two-stream fast-track, and defined one number to decide between them, the 72-hour re-presentation share, patients who return within 72 hours of discharge divided by patients discharged that month, the one outcome on which P and Q were predicted to differ. The committee worked in a hosted project board holding P's proposal, the predictions, and the argument; the board was decommissioned in March 2020 without export, and no copy of P's proposal exists anywhere else. Q was adopted. On 3 November 2017 the quality officer, Rhea Lindqvist, filed the share's definition with the register as the department's quality indicator; the filed definition is, word for word, the text now in the department's dashboard configuration; the filing carries no statement of purpose, and neither the register nor anything at the hospital names Protocol P. The register was built to hold the definition, the hospital, the date, and the officer, and not the purpose. Since January 2018 the hospital has filed the share monthly, and the register publishes only the monthly figure, naming nobody. Because the share is the registered indicator, since January 2018 the department has telephoned every patient counted in it within a week of the return, offered a waiver of the second visit's fee, and asked for a signed release that includes not filing with the State Patient Complaint Docket; a docket hearing is the only setting in which two such patients could learn that they returned for the same cause, since each patient knows only their own return. Between January 2018 and June 2025, 214 releases were signed, no docket complaint concerning a 72-hour return has been filed, and no hearing has convened. No member of the 2017 committee remains, and Lindqvist left in 2019. In August 2025 the current quality manager, Dana Okafor, who joined in 2023, preparing the annual indicator review, reads the definition in the dashboard configuration and in the register, finds them identical and the filing signed by Lindqvist on 3 November 2017, so the definition's source is readable from the arrangement and not inferred, finds nothing at the hospital or in the register saying why this outcome and not another is the indicator, and drafts the review with the share listed as 'legacy indicator, purpose not recorded, recommend retire'.
